meta_description: Configuration management explained: configuration items, the five activities, audits, baselines, how it differs from change control, with a worked example.
excerpt: What configuration management is, the five activities mapped across ISO 10007, APM, PMI and NASA, functional and physical audits, configuration vs project baselines, how CM differs from change and version control, and a calculated worked example following one change.

learning_objectives: Define configuration management and distinguish it from change control, version control and ITIL service configuration management
Name the five CM activities and map them across ISO 10007:2017, APM, PMI and NASA
Select configuration items and version schemes and record their relationships
Explain functional and physical configuration audits and their project equivalents
Distinguish configuration baselines from project baselines
Trace a change's impact through a configuration register and interpret status and audit results

formulas.formula: Share of register = count ÷ total CIs × 100
Items affected = existing CIs revised + new CIs
Audit conformance = matching CIs ÷ CIs audited × 100
Traceability coverage = requirements traced to passed tests ÷ requirements in baseline × 100

unverified_claims: APM attributes its definition to the APM Body of Knowledge 8th edition; the BoK itself was not opened and the edition attribution is APM's

PRINCE2 7 details (issue management approach covering identification, control, status accounting and verification; product register) come from secondary training-provider summaries; the official manual was not accessed
PMI Practice Standard for Project Configuration Management (2007): only the publisher listing and chapter names were seen
SAE EIA-649 (current revision C) described only as widely used in defence and aerospace; the standard text was not accessed
ITIL 4 service configuration management practice and CMDB described in general terms; no ITIL publication was opened
Statement that configuration records for IT components often transfer into a CMDB at project end is general practice, not sourced
